_comment: Manifest for the self-hosted Alaska lidar DEM collection.
target_epsg: the *appropriate local UTM zone*, NAD83(2011) realization.
MatSu is delivered tagged UTM 5N but spans 150.5W - 147.0W, i.e. almost
entirely zone 6 and up to 3 degrees past the zone 5 edge. It is the one
dataset that gets a genuine zone change.
Source datum tags are honored literally (user decision, 2026-09-05):
Lower_KP and MatSu declare WGS 84, so a real WGS84 -> NAD83(2011) datum
transform is applied to them. Homer (NAD83) and KBay (NAD83(2011)) stay
in the NAD83 family. If the WGS84 tags turn out to be a vendor mislabel,
those two will sit ~1-2 m off Homer/KBay and must be rebuilt with an
max_zoom: chosen so one web-mercator pixel ~= one source pixel at that

'gated': true = keep out of the public catalog and off R2 (make_catalog skips it unless --include-gated; r2_sync excludes it); served only behind the admin login once that pathway exists (Hoonah 2015, Corax, Chugachmiut).

datasets.title: Homer 2019 bare-earth DTM
datasets.notes: Source NAD83 / UTM 5N (EPSG:26905), LZW, 128x128 blocks. No vertical CRS declared.
datasets.source: Alaska DGGS — Salisbury, J.B., Daanen, R.P. & Herbst, A.M. (2021), Raw Data File 2021-2; flown for FEMA/City of Homer

datasets.title: Lower Kenai Peninsula lidar DEM
datasets.notes: Source tagged WGS 84 / UTM 5N (EPSG:32605). Uncompressed and stripe-blocked (43603x1) - must be converted to a tiled COG before any windowed read. No vertical CRS declared.
datasets.retired: Superseded 2026-09-17 by kenai_2008, which is the same 2008 survey re-classified from the point cloud. kenai_2008 covers every km2 of this one and 140 km2 more in the same window, and agrees with it to a median of +0.018 m (MAD 0.034 m) over 2.96 M cells at 20 m. The only ground this one has that kenai_2008 does not is 5.7 km2 that is 99.9% below 5 m: water surface the vendor gridded and the ground filter correctly dropped.

datasets.title: Kachemak Bay 2023 lidar DEM
datasets.notes: Arrives as a valid COG (ZSTD, 512 blocks) in a COMPOUND CRS: NAD83(2011) / UTM 5N + NAVD88 height. Already the target horizontal zone, so the archive stage copies rather than warps - warping to a 2D EPSG:6334 would be an identity resample that also silently drops the declared NAVD88 vertical datum. It is the only one of the four that declares its vertical reference. Web tiles rebuilt 2026-09-06: the compound NAVD88 CRS made gdalwarp geoid-shift full-res reads but not overview reads (see CLAUDE.md); the archive now has GDAL-computed overviews (translate mode).
datasets.source: NOAA Office for Coastal Management — AK Coastal Communities (Kachemak Bay) QL1 lidar, collected 2023 (to confirm)

datasets.title: Matanuska Valley 2019 bare-earth DEM
datasets.notes: 82 GB SAGA .sdat, stripe-blocked. No vertical CRS declared. ELEVATIONS ARE IN FEET and are converted to metres on ingest (vertical_scale): the raw grid reads 246.1 at Palmer and 341.5 at Wasilla, whose published elevations are 240 ft and 344 ft - a metres reading would put downtown Palmer at 807 ft. Homer and Lower Kenai agree with each other in metres at an overlap point (19.84 vs 20.06), so the foot units are MatSu's alone. International foot assumed; the US survey foot differs by 2 ppm (3 mm at 1500 m), which is far below the data's own accuracy. Zone-5-tagged but lies in zone 6 - this is the one real reprojection. max_zoom 16 (1.14 m) rather than 17 (0.57 m): 17 would oversample 0.91 m source 1.6x for 4x the bytes. RENAMED 2026-09-12 (Hig): this is the Matanuska corridor; the Susitna side is the 2011 sister blocks. SOURCE FILL: the SAGA grid declares nodata -99999 but holds none; instead 84.5% of the box is exactly 0.00 in one contiguous region outside the lidar swath (a flat 0 m plateau that shaded as real ground). tools/lidar/mask_fill.py --fill 0 turns that region (the zeros connected to the raster border, dilated one coarse cell) into the declared nodata in an intermediate GeoTIFF, /Volumes/Nunatak/lidar_build/matsu_2019/source_masked.tif, which is the build source; genuine 0.00 m pixels inside the swath survive. Raw: /Volumes/Powder/Alaska GIS/Raster/AK_lidar/Matsu_2019/Bare_earth_DEM/2019_MatSu_UTM5.sdat.
datasets.source: U.S. Geological Survey 3DEP — Matanuska-Susitna Borough 2019-2020 QL1 (to confirm)

datasets.title: Matanuska Valley 2011 bare-earth DTM (9 ft)
datasets.notes: Mat-Su Borough 2011 lidar (flown 2011-05-10..12), Matanuska River corridor from Palmer east to ~147.2W. Source is NAD83 / Alaska State Plane zone 4 in US survey feet (FIPS 5004), 9 ft posts, uncompressed, 128x128 blocks. ELEVATIONS ARE IN FEET (metadata: altunits feet, NAVD88 via GEOID09) and are converted to metres on ingest; max 5873 in the raw grid is 1790 m, which is right for the Chugach/Talkeetna summits here and impossible in metres. Verified against matsu_2019 at Palmer airport, Sutton and Chickaloon: 70.78/137.04/414.87 m vs 70.94/137.17/415.10 m. Lies in UTM zone 6. max_zoom 15 (2.27 m) for 2.74 m source.
datasets.source: Matanuska-Susitna Borough 2011 lidar (Matanuska River block)

datasets.title: Seward 2023 bare-earth DTM
datasets.notes: Arrives as a valid COG (LZW, 512 blocks, overviews) in a COMPOUND CRS: NAD83(2011) / UTM 6N + NAVD88 height (GEOID12B), unit metre. Published at 1 m throughout (Hig's call 2026-09-08: 1 m is enough for this purpose; a 0.5 m mosaic came to a 48 GB archive and 6.4 GB of tiles): gdalbuildvrt -resolution user -tr 1 1 -r average, so the 0.5 m units are 2x2-averaged and the 1 m units pass through unchanged; then translate mode. 185 x 145 km box, ~5,500 km2 of data; all NAD83(2011)/UTM 8N; NAVD88 (GEOID12B) per the NOAA InPort records for the project (items 64330/64299); collection spans 2019-2020. Three tile names occur in two units (identical data). max_zoom 16 (1.25 m at 58.6N).

datasets.title: Anchorage 2015 bare-earth DTM (3 ft, MOA / NOAA Digital Coast)
datasets.notes: Municipality of Anchorage 2015 lidar (Merrick, QL2, 957 sq mi), the COMPLETE DEM as republished by NOAA Digital Coast dataset 8431: 51 GeoTIFF tiles of 10240x10240 px at 3 ft in NAD83 / Alaska State Plane zone 4 (US survey feet), NAVD88, Float32 LZW, nodata -9999, 13 GB, downloaded from https://noaa-nos-coastal-lidar-pds.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dem/AK_Anchorage_DEM_2015_8431/ to /Volumes/Nunatak/lidar_src/anchorage_2015/ on 2026-09-11 and mosaicked with gdalbuildvrt. Elevations are in US survey feet, but the tiles DECLARE it (compound CRS '... (ftUS) + NAVD88 height (ftUS)'), so gdalwarp converts them to metres itself; no vertical_scale here. The first build (2026-09-12 overnight) applied the scale as well and shipped heights 0.3048x too small -- caught by Hig as an under-exaggerated surface; rebuilt the same day. Supersedes Hig's partial local set of 308 .img tiles. Lies in UTM zone 6. max_zoom 17 (0.57 m) for 0.91 m source.
datasets.source: Municipality of Anchorage 2015 lidar (Merrick & Co., QL2), republished by NOAA Digital Coast as dataset 8431

datasets.title: Homer 2018 NCMP bare-earth DEM

Sits +0.08 m above homer_2019. NAVD88 per NCMP convention (metadata not local). Second teacher for the Kenai 2008 reprocessing. Units confirmed metres against 3DEP (fit slope 0.99, +0.24 m).

datasets.title: Pedersen Lagoon 2025 multibeam bathymetry
datasets.notes: NPS Water Resources Division / Kenai Fjords NP, EchoBoat 160 uncrewed survey vessel with Norbit iWBMSe multibeam, June 10-12 2025, after the 7 August 2024 landslide-generated tsunami. Source: KEFJ_Pedersen_05m.xyz (positive-down depths, negated here). Gridded by lidar_build/bathy_src/pedersen_merge.py: cell means of the soundings at 0.5/1/2 m, chosen per 2 m block by sounding density (0.5 m where >=95% filled, 1 m >=90%, else 2 m), no interpolation. Metadata states NAVD88 GEOID12B but also that soundings were tide-corrected to MLLW: confirm the vertical datum with NPS before comparing with lidar. NAD83(2011)/UTM 6N.
datasets.source: National Park Service — Water Resources Division and Kenai Fjords National Park

datasets.title: Lituya Bay 2023 preliminary bathymetry
datasets.notes: Preliminary 2023 bathymetry of Lituya Bay, 1 m Float32 GeoTIFF, NAD83(2011)/UTM 8N, NaN nodata, -169 to +6 m. No metadata on disk. Collected by Katie Hughes (Hig, 2026-09-19); fuller attribution pending. VERTICAL RESOLVED 2026-09-19 against lituya_2025 (NOAA H14228), which covers the same seabed. Compared ONLY west of 58.64591 N, -137.57047 W at Hig's direction -- the head and inner basin can genuinely have changed between 2023 and 2025, the outer bay should not have, and restricting to it tightens the core scatter from 0.858 to 0.439 m. On flat bottom (<1 deg, 15,598 pairs) this file sits +0.130 m above H14228's MLLW surface: that is MLLW, not NAVD88, which would have put it 0.513 m BELOW. vertical_shift_m removes both the +0.130 m bias against the NOAA survey and the 0.513 m MLLW-to-NAVD88(GEOID12B) separation. Lituya_PrelimBathy.tif in the same folder is an RGB rendering, not elevations. GATED 2026-09-14 at Hig's request until the originator confirms provenance and vertical datum.
datasets.source: Katie Hughes (fuller attribution pending)

datasets.title: Seldovia 2019 NCMP bare-earth topobathy
datasets.notes: NOAA/USACE National Coastal Mapping Program 2019 (JALBTCX), Seldovia and Seldovia Bay: green lidar, so the grid is continuous from the hills to about -31 m. Source: the 31 vendor BareEarth_1mGrid tiles, mosaicked with a VRT (bathy_src/seldovia_2019_bareearth.vrt); tiles are NAD83(2011) geographic at 0.9e-5 deg (~1 m), warped here to UTM 5N. The companion 1mGrid tiles in the same package are the FIRST-return surface (vegetation kept, +15 m over bare earth at the 90th percentile) and are deliberately not used. Also on disk, not published: 31 classified LAS, 125 RGB orthos, NAVD88 zero contour. Public (NOAA/USACE). VERTICAL: the tiles are labelled NAVD88 but the vendor LAS headers say the heights were computed with xGEOID17B, not the GEOID12B that NAVD88 means elsewhere here, so the delivered surface sits 1.42 m low. vertical_shift_m 1.42 corrects it; see the build_lidar docstring for the evidence and the independent tide-gauge check.
datasets.source: NOAA/USACE National Coastal Mapping Program 2019 (JALBTCX)

datasets.title: Kachemak Bay 2008-2009 multibeam bathymetry
datasets.notes: NOAA hydrographic surveys H11933/34/35/38 (2008) and H12084-90/12114/12146 (2009), the Kachemak Bay 'Hydropalooza'. Built by bathy_proto/stitch_kachemak.py from the per-survey, per-depth-band BASE node lists (Raw/H*/*.xyz), each gridded at its own native cell size (1 m to ~23 m depth, 2 m to ~52 m, 4 m to ~115 m, 8 m below) with no search radius and no interpolation, then stacked finest-on-top into one 1 m VRT: 66 bands, unsurveyed ground left as nodata rather than triangulated across, which is what the vendor's ready-made TIFFs do (32% of one test window was fabricated that way). HORIZONTAL: the node lists carry no CRS, so the grids were written with an override; the survey metadata says NAD83, and the VRT is re-tagged EPSG:6334 without touching pixels (an earlier tag of WGS 84 / UTM 5N would have been ~1 m off in Alaska). VERTICAL: the source is MLLW. vertical_shift_m -1.38 puts it in NAVD88, measured as the median lidar-minus-bathymetry over the two NCMP topobathy surveys that overlap it (2018 Homer -1.334 m over 1.0 M cells, 2019 Seldovia -1.400 m over 2.2 M cells); NOAA Coal Point publishes -1.553 m, and per-2 km blocks run -1.30 to -1.50, so the bay's separation genuinely varies and a constant carries about +/-0.15 m. Matching the lidar is the point, since this exists to be differenced against it. Public (NOAA).
datasets.source: NOAA hydrographic surveys H11933-H11938 (2008) and H12084-H12146 (2009), the Kachemak Bay 'Hydropalooza'; gridded here from the BASE node lists

datasets.title: Prince of Wales Island 2017 lidar DTM
datasets.notes: USGS 3DEP OPR, AK_Prince_of_Wales_Island_QL1_Lidar_2017_B17, 1705 tiles delivered at 0.5 m float32 in NAD83(2011) / UTM 8N. 5,639 km2 of real data inside 6,166 km2 of tile boxes. ARCHIVED AT 1 m, not native: at 0.5 m the archive would be ~27 GB, roughly twice the largest survey in the collection, for a survey nobody has asked for at that resolution; the 0.5 m tiles were kept on disk for a while so any area that later earned it could be rebuilt native, and were RECLAIMED 2026-09-19 (74 GB) once the 1 m archive was verified published on R2 and in the public catalogue. They are not lost: the delivery is USGS 3DEP OPR, AK_Prince_of_Wales_Island_QL1_Lidar_2017_B17, and re-downloadable from rockyweb.usgs.gov. Rebuilding native means fetching 74 GB again, which is the trade that was made. archive_resample average, because a 2x downsample with bilinear samples the target grid instead of integrating the source pixels it skips. HORIZONTAL: the delivery is not uniformly tagged -- 1593 tiles carry EPSG:6337, 91 carry a compound tag with NAVD88 height and 21 carry plain NAD83 from 1986. All three sit interleaved on the same unrotated half-metre lattice, so it is a tagging inconsistency, not three surveys. The VRT re-tags every tile EPSG:6337 without touching a pixel. Left alone the plain-NAD83 tiles would take a NADCON5 datum shift and the compound ones a geoid shift, putting metre-scale steps along arbitrary internal boundaries. Public (USGS).
datasets.source: U.S. Geological Survey 3DEP — AK_Prince_of_Wales_Island_QL1_Lidar_2017_B17

datasets.title: Kenai Peninsula 2008 bare-earth DTM (re-classified)
datasets.product: DTM (bare earth, re-classified from the point cloud)
datasets.notes: USGS 3DEP AK_Kenai_2008 (Aero-Metric, 2008-05-21 to 09-22), 14.05 billion points at ~1.21 pts/m2. No public DTM exists for this survey anywhere, so this one is built here from the points. GROUND CLASSIFICATION: Axelsson progressive TIN densification (r-lidar's MIT C++ library, driven from PDAL by tools/lidar/ptd_ground), angle 40, distance 3, seed 10 m, outlier detection off. Chosen on a hand-scored test patch against the 2019 QL1 surface: crest loss 11.9% against the vendor classification's 20.5%, the tightest spread and fewest gross errors of six candidates, and the least false roughness under dense canopy. 3,130 tiles of 2 km with a 30 m classification buffer, 6.37 h on 8 cores, no failures. Grids are snapped to a GLOBAL 4 ft lattice: a 2 km tile is 1640.42 cells, so pinning each raster to its own tile bounds put neighbours up to 51 cm out of step and would have seamed the mosaic. Agreement with the independent Homer 2019 survey, both warped to one 5 m lattice over their 39.9 x 14.9 km overlap: median -0.014 m, MAD 0.092 m over 3.6 M cells, 1.21% of cells differing by more than 2 m. The entire >20 m tail is 228 cells in a single 1 km spot at 59.65913,-151.67076, material missing from 108 m and added at 24 m nearby -- ground that moved between the surveys, not an artifact. DESPIKED after gridding (tools/lidar/despike_dtm.py): two tests, because neither catches both artifacts -- an iterative 5x5-median test for the low spikes that outlier detection would have caught, and a scale-free support test for clouds and bird flocks, which asks whether a blob's lowest cell clears the 90th percentile of its own rim rather than how high it is, so a 1800 m arete survives and a blob hanging in the air does not. The classified point cloud is kept on Powder so the gridding can be redone without reclassifying. dev_only until reviewed. Public (USGS).
datasets.source: NOAA National Geodetic Survey, Remote Sensing Division — Integrated Ocean and Coastal Mapping (IOCM) lidar, 2008; distributed by USGS 3DEP as AK_Kenai_2008. Bare-earth surface classified here from the delivered points.

datasets.title: Index Lake 2024 drone DSM (Corax)
datasets.notes: Corax Drone Services 2024 instability survey, photogrammetric DSM at 0.1444 m in NAD83(2011) / UTM 6N, NAVD88 heights per the filename. Source is stripe-blocked (one row of blocks the full width, 32 rows tall), so a windowed read has to pull a whole stripe -- it is converted to a tiled COG before anything else touches it. The CRS arrives as a BOUNDCRS wrapping EPSG:6335 with an all-zero NAD83(2011)->WGS84 transform, so src_srs re-tags it to plain 6335 (NAD83(2011) / UTM 6N; the series starts at 6330 for zone 1N, so 6332 is zone 3N and puts these sites off the Yukon Delta): identical geometry, and it stops a warp from inventing a datum shift. This is a SURFACE model (first return: canopy, buildings, boulders), not bare earth -- which is the point, since the survey is of boulders and slope instability. GATED: not a public delivery. FILL MODE 'holes': the default leaves a void inside a tile the survey touches unfilled, which is right for a coastal lidar survey where a void is water the sensor could not see. Here it is wrong -- a void is simply outside the flight polygon, and because a z13 tile is 2.3 km across while the survey is 1.6-2.6 km, leaving it unfilled wrapped each site in a flat 0 m collar most of a tile wide, which also pulled the 3D camera onto a false plane. ORTHO: the matching orthomosaic is built by build_ortho.py to <id>_ortho.pmtiles and carried in the catalogue as ortho_url, so the viewer can drape it over this DSM. Imagery and surface come from the same flight and are only interpretable together -- an SfM ortho draped over anything else is draped over the wrong shape.
datasets.source: Corax Drone Services LLC (private delivery)

datasets.title: MNI 2023 lidar DTM (Corax)
datasets.notes: Corax Drone Services 2023, the fourth site of the same collection as the 2024 Index Lake / Muddy Creek / Upper Boulder Creek packages, but delivered separately and by a different method: this one is LIDAR, not photogrammetry, which is why it has no orthomosaic and why it is a bare-earth DTM rather than a surface model. UNITS: the delivery ships three copies of one surface and only one is usable directly. Corax2023_6393usfeet.tif (NAD83(2011) / Alaska Albers) and its _UTM6 reprojection both carry ELEVATIONS IN US SURVEY FEET -- 2334 to 4989 -- while Corax2023_UTM6_m.tif is the same ground in metres, 711 to 1521; the ratio is 3.2809, which is the US survey foot to four decimal places rather than the international foot. The metres copy is the source here, so no vertical conversion is needed and none can be got wrong. HORIZONTAL: that copy is tagged WGS 84 / UTM 6N, which is the reprojection's error -- the authoritative Albers original is NAD83(2011) -- so src_srs re-tags it EPSG:6335 to match the rest of the collection. The re-tag guard confirms the footprint does not move. No orthomosaic was delivered with this site, unlike the 2024 three. GATED: not a public delivery; provenance is a letter of commitment, not an open licence. ZOOM: z20, not the z19 that rounding to the nearest zoom gives. At 61.8N a z19 pixel is 0.141 m and this survey is 0.105 m, so z19 would serve it 1.35x coarser than it was flown -- throwing away a third of the detail that makes it worth gating. The other Corax sites land within 2% of native at their rounded zoom; this one sits just above a zoom boundary, which is exactly where rounding to nearest costs the most.
datasets.source: Corax Drone Services LLC (private delivery)

datasets.title: Dixon 2023 SfM surface model (USFWS)
datasets.notes: Structure-from-motion survey of 19 September 2023 from Mark Laker, covering the south side of Kachemak Bay around Dixon and Grewingk. 0.30 m surface model over a 31 x 23 km box of which 64.5% carries data -- about 409 km2, which makes it far the largest SfM survey in the collection. Elevations 45 to 1730 m; the delivery states no vertical datum and none is embedded, so it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed at. DATE: the orthomosaic tiles are named Dixon_09192024 against the DSM's 09192023, which looks like a year's gap between surface and imagery and is not one -- every file in the package, both products, was written on 2024-07-02, which is BEFORE 19 September 2024. The ortho name is a typo; both come from the 2023 flight, which is what makes draping the imagery on this surface legitimate. ORTHO SOURCE: Ortho_merge.tif in the package is 76 GB of zeros -- a merge that failed silently and was kept. Five full-resolution windows across the middle of it are empty. The imagery is built instead from the 214 tiles in Ortho/, via a VRT. Produced by Mark Laker of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Kenai National Wildlife Refuge, and published here with his agreement. VERTICAL DATUM: the delivery is in NAD83(2011) ELLIPSOIDAL heights, not NAVD88, and says nothing either way. Measured on the terrain that can settle it -- 700-1100 m, slope under 4 degrees, on the 4,368 cells where this survey, kbay_2023, grewingk_2021 and USGS 3DEP all have data -- Dixon sits +10.38 m (MAD 0.36) above 3DEP while grewingk_2021 sits at -0.02 and kbay_2023 at +0.09. The offset matches the geoid separation here, so the source is converted ONCE with a real vertical transform (EPSG:6335+6319 -> EPSG:6335+5703, which PROJ resolves over Alaska to the GEOID12B grid us_noaa_g2012ba0 at a stated 0.02 m -- the same model grewingk_2021 records) rather than shifted by a constant: the geoid runs from +9.69 m at the north-west corner to +11.63 m at the south-east, so a single number would leave nearly two metres of tilt across the survey. A WARNING FOR THE NEXT COMPARISON: kbay_2023 first appeared to be the broken one, 10 m high, because gdalwarp silently applies a geoid shift to a source whose CRS is compound -- and kbay_2023 is the one survey here that declares its vertical datum. Pass -novshiftgrid when measuring against it, or measure the warp instead of the data. The converted file keeps a compound CRS declaring NAVD88, so archive_mode 'translate' is used rather than any warp: gdal_translate preserves the vertical declaration, and a src_srs re-tag would silently drop it. ONE ORTHO TILE IS DAMAGED. Dixon_09192024-9-11.tif fails LZW decoding and stopped the first build; a scan of all 214 found it is the only one, and the damage is a single 32-row strip. Dropping the tile would have cost 1500 x 1500 m of imagery for a fault occupying 5 m, so it is copied block by block with the unreadable strip written as nodata: 0.32% of that tile, 0.0075 km2 of a 409 km2 survey. The repaired copy lives beside the VRT. Note that it must carry RGB colour interpretation or gdalbuildvrt drops it SILENTLY with a warning about heterogeneous bands and rebuilds the hole you were trying to avoid.
datasets.source: Mark Laker, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service — Kenai National Wildlife Refuge

datasets.title: Portage slope 2022 SfM surface model
datasets.vertical_datum: NAVD88 (matches portage_2020 to 0.2 m; none stated in the record)
datasets.source: Lemaire, E., Dufresne, A., Higman, B. & Hamdi, P. (RWTH Aachen University) — CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.14548600
datasets.region: Turnagain Arm and Prince William Sound
datasets.notes: Structure-from-motion survey of the Portage slope, flown 10 August 2022, from the open Zenodo record 'Portage slope 2022 and 2023 DEMs' (CC BY 4.0). 0.25 m, about 2.9 km2 of data inside a 2.6 x 2.7 km box. Downloaded and checksum-verified against the record (7ccaf76c). SOURCE QUIRKS: Float64 and uncompressed with one-row strips, so it is converted once to a tiled Float32 COG -- a DEM has no use for 15 significant figures and the strip layout makes every windowed read pull the full width. Nodata is declared as 18.58, an odd value that turns out to be safe: it sits below the lowest real elevation here (26 m), so no ground is masked by it. HORIZONTAL: declared WGS 84 / UTM 6N, so it is REPROJECTED to NAD83(2011) / UTM 6N rather than re-tagged -- the two differ by about a metre in Alaska and the declaration is the only evidence available. VERTICAL: no datum stated, and none needed. Against portage_2020 (NAVD88 lidar over the same slope) the medians are -0.17 m (2022) and -0.18 m (2023) on ground under 2 degrees, with no sign of the ~10 m offset an ellipsoidal product would show. The offset is NOT flat across slope bands (-0.17 at <2 deg, -0.45 at <5, -0.04 at <20), which is what rules out a constant datum bias: the residual is the slope moving and SfM noise, and half the gentle-ground cells differ by more than a metre between 2022 and 2023. 3DEP is no use as a reference here -- even portage_2020 sits 24 m from it, because the 2010 IfSAR predates a lot of glacier change in this valley.

datasets.title: Pedersen 2024 SfM surface model (NPS)
datasets.vertical_datum: NAVD88 (GEOID12B), stated in the delivery metadata
datasets.source: National Park Service — Alaska Regional Office, Natural Resources Team, and Kenai Fjords National Park
datasets.notes: Structure-from-motion survey of the Pedersen Glacier / Pedersen Lagoon landslide, flown 9 August 2024 by the National Park Service, one year after the 7 August 2024 landslide-generated tsunami that pedersen_2025 surveys the seabed of. 0.341 m surface model with a 0.17 m orthomosaic. GATED, and not because the data is sensitive: the delivery states that it 'cannot be further distributed in its original form without approval of the NPS and all products derived from it must identify the NPS as the source'. The web pyramid and the ortho tiles are derived renderings and are fine to serve with NPS credited; the archive COG is the original form and is NOT to be published until the NPS says so. Hig is asking (contact in the delivery: Chad Hults, Alaska NPS Regional Geologist). Until then the whole survey stays behind the gate, which is the conservative reading. DATUM: stated outright for once -- NAD83(2011) epoch 2010, Alaska State Plane 4, NAVD88 Geoid 12B Alaska, with a vertical RMSE of 0.109 m and a mean error of 0.002 m against 20 GNSS check points. No datum work needed, unlike Dixon. SOURCE CHOICE: the delivery ships the DSM three times. The _UTM6 copy is tagged WGS 84 / UTM 6N, which contradicts the metadata and is 3x the size; the native copy is NAD83(2011) / Alaska zone 4 exactly as documented. The native one is the source here, reprojected once to UTM 6N and written Float32 -- a projection change inside one datum, so no pixel values move. The orthomosaic stays in Alaska zone 4 and is tiled from there (build_ortho --srs keep), because the tiler reprojects to Web Mercator regardless and re-tagging a correct State Plane file as UTM 6N would move the imagery a long way while looking like housekeeping. ZOOM: z18, which is 0.30 m here against a 0.341 m source. z19 was set by hand at first and is wrong twice over -- it is 2.3x finer than the data, and it makes the terrain-RGB encode a 93708 x 93536 raster, which is what killed the first build.

datasets.title: Prince of Wales Island 2018 lidar DTM
datasets.source: U.S. Geological Survey 3DEP
datasets.notes: USGS 3DEP OPR, AK_PrinceOfWalesP2_2018_B18: 1145 tiles at 0.5 m in NAD83(2011) / UTM 8N. Unlike the 2017 delivery this one is uniform -- every tile EPSG:6337, 0.5 m, Float32, nodata -999999, 256-square blocks, LZW -- so no re-tagging is needed and the VRT is a straight mosaic. ARCHIVED AT NATIVE 0.5 m, unlike pow_2017, which was downsampled to 1 m because 0.5 m over its 5,670 km2 would have made a 27 GB archive. This block is a third of that area, so native costs roughly what 2017 cost at half the resolution. max_zoom 18 is 0.33 m here, finer than the source; z17 would be 0.67 m, a third coarser than flown. OVERLAPS pow_2017, which is the interesting part: 2017 spans -133.82..-132.28 / 55.02..56.36 and this spans -134.44..-131.12 / 54.80..57.11, so where they meet there is a 2017-to-2018 pair for the difference tool, and beyond it this adds coverage 2017 never had.

datasets.title: Grewingk Lake 2023 sonar bathymetry (1 m)
datasets.source: Katie Hughes (fuller attribution pending)
datasets.notes: Grewingk Lake bed, surveyed 2023-05-18/19 from a boat with a Qinsy-logged sonar; the delivered 1 m grid (896x1152, ~1.0 km2 of tile box, 29% of it surveyed) sits beside 107 raw .las swaths totalling 1.4 GB, which would support a finer regrid if anyone wants one. DATUM, unusually, is not in doubt: the LAS headers carry a full compound CRS -- NAD83(2011)/UTM 5N + NAVD88 height, geoid model GEOID12B A0 (Alaska), written by Qinsy -- while the delivered GeoTIFF is tagged EPSG:6334 with no vertical CRS. Cross-checked against grewingk_2021, which covers the same water: the 2021 lidar reads a flat plane at 48.55 m over 76% of this footprint (a proglacial lake's surface as seen from the air), and the shallowest sonar return is 47.45 m, 1.10 m below it -- boat draft plus two years of lake level, where an ellipsoid/geoid mix-up here would be about 10 m. No dry ground is in common, so that is a gross-error check, not a sub-metre tie. Values are lake-bed ELEVATIONS (18.19 to 47.45 m), not depths, so the deepest point is ~29 m below the 2021 surface. GATED 2026-09-19 at Hig's request pending fuller attribution from the surveyor; the same surveyor's lituya_2023 is gated for the same reason. max_zoom 17 (0.60 m).

datasets.title: Lituya Bay 2025 multibeam bathymetry (1 m)
datasets.source: NOAA Office of Coast Survey - hydrographic survey H14228, NOAA Ship RAINIER, July 2025, with the National Park Service
datasets.notes: NOAA Ship RAINIER, surveyed 2025-07-23 to 07-28 with NPS for Glacier Bay National Park; the first survey of Lituya Bay since 1959. Delivered as one variable-resolution BAG (H14228_MB_VR_MLLW_1of1, 251 MB, 1.01-4.05 m), extracted here to a uniform 1 m grid via the BAG driver's INTERPOLATED mode: 16384x16384, 46.7 km2 of real soundings. (First published 2026-09-19 from RESAMPLED_GRID, which recovered only 29.0 km2 -- that mode samples refinement nodes, so cells between them come back empty wherever the refinement is coarser than 1 m. Rebuilt 2026-09-20.) Values run -134.6 to +0.91 m relative to MLLW. Already NAD83(2011)/UTM 8N (EPSG:6337), so no re-tag. VERTICAL: the BAG is MLLW depth (EPSG:5866). MLLW sits 0.513 m below NAVD88(GEOID12B) here, applied as vertical_shift_m. Derived through BlueTopo, which is built from this same survey and carries it in NAVD88: MLLW to NAVD88(xGEOID17B) = 1.164 m (23,868 gentle-seabed pairs, std 0.039, 64 percent in one 5 cm bin), less GEOID12B-vs-xGEOID17B = 0.651 m (14,644 land pairs on <2 deg slope against glacier_bay_2019, core std 0.145). CORRECTION 2026-09-20: an earlier note claimed Yakutat's CO-OPS datums corroborated this to 7.7 cm. That compared feet against metres -- Yakutat publishes NAVD88-MLLW = +0.590 FEET = +0.180 m, which is 0.33 m from the chained value, not 0.08 m. Yakutat is 160 km away with a different tidal range, so a difference of that size is unremarkable, but it is not corroboration: the BlueTopo chain stands on its own measurements. No tide station exists in Lituya Bay (nearest is Tarr Inlet, 57 km, inside Glacier Bay), so the benchmark route that settled Resurrection Bay is unavailable here. NOTE the intertidal tie that usually settles these does NOT exist here: glacier_bay_2019 over this water is 36 percent hydro-flattened to 0.00 m and the rest is the flight-time sea surface (a plane at 0.82 m, std 0.089), not ground, so the two instruments share no common surface. max_zoom 17 (0.62 m).

datasets.title: Resurrection Bay 2016 multibeam bathymetry (1 m)
datasets.source: NOAA Office of Coast Survey - hydrographic survey F00683, NOAA Ship RAINIER, 2016
datasets.notes: NOAA Ship RAINIER, 2016; the broader of the two Resurrection Bay surveys, 72.7 km2 of soundings from Seward south down the bay. Delivered as five fixed-resolution BAGs (1/2/4/8/16 m) covering the same footprint at different densities, stacked finest-on-top into one 1 m VRT -- the same structure and treatment as kachemak_bathy_2009. Depths to -294.6 m. RESOLUTION IS MOSTLY COARSE, and the 1 m grid does not change that: by sounded area the bands are 16 m 63.0 percent, 8 m 20.4, 4 m 9.7, 2 m 4.3, 1 m only 2.6 -- the fine data is inshore, the deep basin is 16 m. The VRT reads its sources BILINEAR, not nearest: replicating each 16 m cell into 256 one-metre cells drew a staircase (61.5 percent of cells in a test window had exactly zero gradient, with 6 m steps at the block edges) rather than a seabed. Bilinear drops that to 0.3 percent while leaving mean relief almost unchanged, and being a convex combination of four neighbours it cannot overshoot into pits the soundings do not contain -- which cubic can. max_zoom still follows the 1 m band, so deep water is displayed far finer than it was measured; read detail there as interpolation, not survey. HORIZONTAL: tagged EPSG:32606 (WGS 84 / UTM 6N), not NAD83; PROJ treats WGS84 -> NAD83(2011) as a null shift, the same situation as homer_2018, where a Nuth & Kaab fit showed ~0.2 m residual. VERTICAL: the BAGs are MLLW depth. MLLW sits 0.118 m below NAVD88(GEOID12B) here, applied as vertical_shift_m. Determined from the tide station's own bench mark tie, which is the only route that works in south-central: mark '5090 E 1982' is 5.231 m above MLLW on the CO-OPS bench mark sheet for 9455090, and the same disk (NGS PID DQ3873) is 5.113 m above NAVD88 by GPS (NAD83(2011) ellipsoid 17.147 m minus GEOID12B 12.034 m). Same physical mark, two datums. CO-OPS does not publish a NAVD88 row for Seward because that needs two or more marks with NGS elevations and only this one has a datasheet -- the rest carry OPUS PIDs, a different database. Cross-check: this implies MSL-NAVD88 = 1.576 m, inside the 1.237-1.737 m range of the six nearest stations publishing both. NOTE none of the usual routes work here: VDatum has only three Alaska regions (all Southeast), PROJ offers only a no-shift ballpark, BlueTopo stops at -138 deg, and seward_2023 is topographic lidar that stops at the waterline -- its lowest value (-1.20 m NAVD88) sits above the sonar's shallowest (-0.04 m MLLW), so the two never measure common ground. max_zoom 17 (0.60 m).
